subject.title: [Feature]: Native E2EE Browser Chat, No Third-Party Required

question: Should OpenClaw pursue native browser-held E2EE chat in core now, or first define Gateway/plugin APIs and leave the transport outside core until maintainers sponsor it?
rationale: This changes security boundaries, Gateway chat protocol, browser UX, routing, transcript storage, and the core/plugin ownership model; automation cannot choose that product/security direction safely.

options.title: Design the E2EE architecture and API seam first
options.body: Keep the issue open for a maintainer-owned design covering key lifecycle, encrypted envelopes, transcript semantics, fallback relay behavior, and whether a plugin can own the transport.

options.title: Sponsor a core-native implementation
options.body: Accept that OpenClaw core will own the browser E2EE transport and require security review plus broad Gateway/UI/protocol tests before code lands.

options.title: Defer to external plugin/ClawHub delivery
options.body: Keep core lean and ask for an external plugin only after confirming current or new plugin APIs can support the required encrypted chat behavior.

recommendation.title: Design the E2EE architecture and API seam first
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open for a maintainer-owned design covering key lifecycle, encrypted envelopes, transcript semantics, fallback relay behavior, and whether a plugin can own the transport.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the prior keep-open review and has adjacent Gateway/Control UI chat history, making him the best available decision router from the traced owners.
